💡 Key Takeaways
  • A cashless store is legal in most of the U.S., since federal law leaves it to each store whether to take cash.
  • In a recent development, the “legal tender for all debts, public and private” line on every bill reads like a rule that stores must take it.
  • Legal tender means cash is a valid way to pay a debt, the Federal Reserve explains, but no federal law requires a private business to take it for a purchase.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A cashless store is legal in most of the U.S., since federal law leaves it to each store whether to take cash. But 10 states, and cities such as Philadelphia and San Francisco, require most stores and restaurants to accept it. Check your state’s and city’s rules before you count on paying cash, and carry a backup card.

In a recent development, the “legal tender for all debts, public and private” line on every bill reads like a rule that stores must take it. It isn’t one.

Legal tender means cash is a valid way to pay a debt, the Federal Reserve explains, but no federal law requires a private business to take it for a purchase.

In a recent development, in November 2026, the Pew Research Center counted 10 states that make most in-person businesses take cash: Massachusetts, Fresh Jersey, Rhode Island, Colorado, Connecticut, Oregon, Delaware, Montana, New York, and Maryland. New York’s law took effect in March 2026 and Maryland’s in October, and Illinois’s starts in January 2028. Pew counted 10 cities and counties too, including Philadelphia, San Francisco, Detroit, Miami-Dade County, and Washington, D.C.

Before you insist on paying cash, know what your law leaves out. The laws mostly cover stores and restaurants, but Connecticut’s law exempts membership warehouse clubs such as Costco, Oregon’s exempts farmers markets and roadside stands, and New York’s lets a store turn down bills over $20. Some, New York’s among them, also exempt a store with a kiosk that turns cash into a prepaid card, which in New York must be free to use.

Industry observers note that if a store your law covers still refuses your cash, ask for a manager and mention the law. If that fails, report the store to the office that enforces it, such as New York’s attorney general.

In a recent development, where no law applies, a card-only venue may offer one of those kiosks anyway. Say a stadium’s concession stands take only cards and its kiosk turns your $20 into a prepaid card. Look for a fee on its screen before you insert the bill, and use up the balance, since some prepaid cards charge a fee once they sit unused.

Keep a debit card from a free checking account, or a prepaid card with no monthly fee, in your wallet next to your cash, so you can still pay where cash isn’t taken.

Compare the best free checking accounts for a debit card with no monthly fee.

Do you think a million-dollar term life insurance policy sounds like too much insurance?

As a Certified Financial Planner, I see underinsured people every day.

A million-dollar term life insurance policy might actually be the minimum coverage needed for the typical middle-class household, but it’s affordable.

That might sound like an exaggeration, but if you crunch the numbers – just as we’ll be doing a little bit – you’ll realize that a million-dollar policy might be just what you need.

The good news is term life insurance isn’t nearly as costly as most people think.

Industry observers note that what makes term life insurance even better is that larger policies cost less on a per thousand basis than smaller policies do. You may find the premium on a $1 million policy is only a little bit higher than it is for $500,000.

Probably, but let’s find out. A general rule of thumb is that you should get 10x your income as baseline coverage for life insurance.

If you’re young, that may be low because you may want to provide your family with enough to replace your income for 15 years or more.

Today, $1 million has become the latest baseline for life insurance by a primary breadwinner. Anything less could leave your family financially impaired.

Here’s a list of all the different obligations you may want to have life insurance cover in the unfortunate event you pass away early.

Now that you have an idea of these obligations, let’s punch them into this life insurance calculator to find out if you need a million-dollar policy.

According to Policy Genius, the average cost for a 20-year $1 million term life insurance policy for a 35-year-old male is $53 per month. However, your rate will vary according to the following factors.

According to recent reports, the best, and easiest place to start is online. I recommend having two or three insurers compete for your business to make sure you get the best rate and coverage. Let’s look at the individual components that can promptly add up to over a million-dollar policy.

This is where things can get a bit intimidating. Even if you earn a modest income, you may need close to $1 million to replace that income after your death in order to provide for your family’s basic living expenses.

Recent findings suggest that the conventional wisdom in the insurance industry is that you should maintain a life insurance policy equal to between 10 times and 20 times your annual income. So if you earn around $50K per year, that would mean policy coverage between $500K and $1 million.

The complication today is that with interest rates being as low as they are that might not be enough either.

For example, if you have a $1 million policy that could be invested at 5% per year, your family could live on the interest earned – which conveniently comes to $50,000 per year – for the next 20 years.

In a recent development, that would still leave the original $1 million intact to cover other expenses. But with today’s microscopic interest rates, there’s no way to get a guaranteed return of 5% on your money, certainly not for 15 or 20 years.

Recent findings suggest that also, keep in mind that most insurance companies have a maximum multiplier you can apply to your income for life insurance coverage. For example, it wouldn’t make much sense for a 22-year-old making $27,000 per year to get a $2 million life insurance. Or a 65-year-old that is retired to secure a $3 million dollar policy.

The table below is approximately how much you’re allowed to multiply your income based on your age and income:.

Here we start with the basics – wrapping up your final affairs.

This will include funeral costs and any lingering medical costs. A reasonable estimate for a typical funeral is around $20,000.

Crazy, right? You can get burial insurance to cover only the most basic of final expenses.

Sources indicate that debt burdens are high in the US, and debt can be especially crushing on remaining family members. Many life insurance customers make sure they can pay off most of their debt with the policy.

Medical costs are a serious variable. Even if you have excellent health insurance, there are likely to be unpaid medical bills lingering after your death. This has to do with copayments, deductibles, and coinsurance provisions.

Recent findings suggest that collectively, they can add up to many thousands of dollars. But where things get really complicated is if you die of a terminal illness.

Sources indicate that for example, if you are stricken by an illness that lasts for several years, you could incur a number of expenses that are not covered by insurance. This may include the cost of personal care and even experimental treatments.

Sources indicate that A home may be a large asset, but it’s also often a homeowner’s largest debt. The average mortgage balance in the US is roughly $236,443 according to Experian data. So you could easily use a life insurance policy to pay off that debt and relieve your loved ones of a monthly mortgage payment.

Sources indicate that credit card debt and other personal debt are some of the most expensive obligations carrying rates upward of 20% in some cases. Make sure you have enough to cover this very expensive debt.

Below is a sampling of major expenses your family is likely to incur, either on an annual basis or at some point after your death.

According to recent reports, tuition costs continue to skyrocket. The Department of Education suggests that four-year public college tuition has been rising an average of 5% per year, far exceeding the rate of inflation. If you have one child who attends an in-state public school, a second at an out-of-state public school, and a third in a private university, the total expenditure will reach $416,560.

Vehicles and other forms of transportation represent another large sum. Unfortunately, with increasing electronics and safety features, the average cost of a newly introduced car continues to grow.

If your family relies on your work for healthcare, take notice. According to eHealth.com, the average health insurance premium for a family is $22,221. That’s a shade under $2,000 per month in additional cost. This cost will only rise, and the need could last for years.

So far, we’ve been describing the financial obligations likely to affect a typical household.But there may be certain situations that will produce obligations that are less obvious.

For example, if you’re a business owner, there may be debts or other financial obligations that will need to be paid upon your death.

Even though no one in your family may be qualified or interested in taking over your business, the payoff of those obligations may be completely necessary to enable the sale of the business.

Another possibility is that you’re a real estate investor.

If your properties are heavily indebted, extra insurance proceeds may be necessary either to carry the properties until they’re sold, or even to pay off existing indebtedness to free up cash flow for income.

You may even need additional funds if you are taking care of an extended family member, like an aging parent.

These are just some of the many possibilities of expenses that will need to be covered by insurance proceeds.

Before we move on to specific life insurance quotes, let’s first consider the factors that affect term life insurance premiums.

Sources indicate that this is typically the single most crucial premium factor. The older you are, the more likely you are to die within the term of the policy.

This is a close second and why it’s so notable to apply for a policy as early in life as possible. Premiums on life insurances rates literally increase by each year.

In a recent development, if you have any health conditions that may affect mortality, such as diabetes or hypertension, your premiums will be higher. This is another compelling reason to apply while you are young and in good health.

It’s not that policies are not available to people with health conditions, it’s just that they’re less expensive if you don’t have any.

A 10-year term policy will have a lower premium than a 20-year term policy, which will be lower than a 30-year term. The shorter the term, the less likely it is the insurance tech giant will have to pay a claim before it expires.

Size of the policy matters, but not the way you might think. Yes, a $1 million policy will cost more than a $500,000 policy. But it won’t cost twice as much.

The larger the policy, the lower the per-thousand cost will be.

When the size of the death benefit is considered, the larger policy will always be more cost-effective.

Recent findings suggest that for example, certain occupations are more hazardous than others (think policeman versus librarian). Deep-sea diving is higher risk than golf. And smoking is the one activity guaranteed to raise your premiums substantially.

With this information in mind, let’s take a look at whether you should consider a $1 million whole life policy instead.

Recent findings suggest that any discussion on life insurance should include a comparison of whole life and term life insurance coverage. After all, both products can be immensely valuable in the right situation, yet one product (whole life) costs considerably more than the other.

Most of the time, the debate is settled in favor of term life insurance based on cost alone.

A whole life insurance policy can easily cost 10x the same amount of coverage you can get with a term policy.

With that being remarked, whole life insurance and other investment-type life insurance coverage can be valuable in terms of the cash value you can build up over time. Whole life insurance also offers a fixed benefit amount for your heirs that will last for your entire life, yet the cost of your premiums are guaranteed to stay the same.

Industry observers note that the cash value of a whole life insurance policy also grows on a tax-deferred basis, and you can borrow against this amount if you need a loan. Further, many whole life policies from reputable providers also pay out dividends during good years, which can be substantial.

The problem with whole life and other similar policies like universal life is the fact that premiums can be exorbitant for the amount of coverage you might need.

A couple with young children provides a good example since they might need a $1 million dollar policy or more to provide income protection for their working years and have money left for college tuition and other expenses.

With young families, expenses are already high.

This includes costs for food for a family, childcare, heavy use of health care, and the seemingly endless demand for clothing, furniture, and even entertainment as the children grow.

As you can see from the cost comparison below from State Farm, there’s not enough room in the typical family budget to afford the type of life insurance that’s needed.

A 40-year-old mother and breadwinner in excellent health would pay $80.09 per month for a term life policy that lasts 20 years, whereas a whole life policy in the same amount would cost $1,266.69 per month (or $14,560 annually).

Recent findings suggest that this is a classic situation where term insurance rides to the rescue. The family can afford to buy the amount of coverage they need at an affordable price, whereas paying for permanent life insurance coverage in the same amount would be difficult to justify.

And just as important for people of any age and in any circumstance, the extra funds not being spent on insurance premiums can be invested to gradually improve your financial situation.

So absolutely, term insurance will work best for most people.

Once again, you get a $200 drop in the annual premium by losing another 10 years on the term.

Holiday hosts can save more by buying the Thanksgiving turkey from the grocery ads and spending New Year’s Eve at home rather than going out.

Industry observers note that before you buy a rental or turn your home into one, add up every cost of owning it, from the mortgage and taxes to repairs, empty months, and management. Go ahead only if the rent covers them all with room to spare and you’re ready to screen tenants, follow landlord-tenant laws, and take repair calls.

According to recent reports, rent that beats the mortgage payment doesn’t make a rental profitable. The gap has to pay for everything else the property costs.

In a recent development, say a couple rents out their old condo, and its mortgage payment, property taxes and insurance included, is $1,600 a month. At $1,900 in rent, they expect to clear $300 a month, or $3,600 a year. Then two empty months cost $3,800 in rent, and a new water heater and a cleaning between tenants cost $3,200. They end the year $3,400 behind.

Before you buy, or rent out the home you’re leaving, budget for four more costs:.

Depreciation lowers the tax on your rent because you deduct the building’s cost, though not the land’s, over 27.5 years. The IRS also lets owners who approve tenants and repairs deduct up to $25,000 a year of rental losses from other income, an allowance that shrinks to nothing at higher incomes. Any loss beyond it waits for a later year.

It has been revealed that A rental is also a job. Someone has to screen applicants, follow fair housing rules and your state’s security deposit and eviction laws, and take the midnight call about a leak. That’s you, or a manager you pay. A real estate fund gives you a stake in property without that work, so count your time as a cost too.

Become a landlord only if the rent still leaves money after every cost above, with repairs and management figured at the high end of their ranges.

Free calculators, a personalized FI roadmap, and a community of 25K+ on the same journey.

One of the highest-value redemptions in travel rewards.

It has been revealed that picture this: you're settling into a lie-flat business class seat somewhere over the Atlantic, a glass of something cold in hand, knowing that in 48 hours you'll be waking up in Istanbul — and then, a few days later, continuing onward to Bangkok. Two bucket-list cities. One award booking. One points balance. This is what the Aeroplan stopover sweet spot feels like in practice. It's not a trick or a loophole — it's a deliberately designed feature of Air Canada's Aeroplan program that the vast majority of travelers simply don't know exists. And that gap between awareness and reality is exactly where the ChooseFI community finds its edge. Here's the math that should make your jaw drop. A business class itinerary from North America to Istanbul with a continuing flight onward to Bangkok — two long-haul segments, lie-flat seats, Star Alliance lounges at every connection — would cost somewhere between **$6,000 and $15,000 in cash**. That's a realistic retail range depending on season and how far out you book. Most people never consider it a possibility for a family vacation or a milestone trip because the sticker price puts it in a different universe. With Aeroplan, you're booking that same itinerary — the same seats, the same lounges, the same Turkish Airlines or Thai Airways product — for **75,000 Aeroplan points**. At the low end of the cash price range, that's already **8 cents per point**. At the high end, you're extracting **20 cents per point** from a currency that most people earned by putting groceries on a credit card. The pricing inefficiency here is structural. Aeroplan's partner award chart prices long-haul business class at a fixed rate regardless of cash fare fluctuations. When business class prices spike — around holidays, during peak travel seasons, during major events — your points cost stays exactly the same. You're insulated from the market. That's the FI mindset applied to travel: you've already paid for the trip in points, slowly accumulated through everyday spending, and now you're simply redeeming the stored value. The stopover itself is nearly free. Aeroplan charges just 5,000 extra miles to add a stopover city to a one-way award. That means your Istanbul layover becomes a multi-day stay — at zero additional points cost beyond that small add-on — and you haven't booked a second award at all. One booking. Two destinations. That's the entire premise, and once you see it, you can't unsee it.

The mechanism behind this sweet spot is elegantly simple once you understand it, but it requires knowing three things that most travelers don't: how Aeroplan's routing rules work, what a stopover actually is in the context of an award ticket, and why Star Alliance's global network makes this scalable to almost any destination pair you can imagine.

When Aeroplan relaunched its loyalty program in 2020, it did something remarkable: it eliminated fuel surcharges entirely and published a partner award chart with fixed pricing for flights on Star Alliance carriers. This is critical. When you book Turkish Airlines business class through Aeroplan, you pay the Aeroplan fixed chart rate — not what Turkish Airlines would charge in its own currency or miles program, and not the inflated cash price. That fixed chart is the engine of this redemption.

Industry observers note that for long-haul international business class, Aeroplan's chart prices routing through multiple regions based on your origin and destination — not every intermediate stop. This is the aha moment. Aeroplan determines your award price based on where your journey starts and where it ends, and then allows you to add a stopover in between for just 5,000 additional miles. The stopover city is priced as a pass-through for the purpose of calculating your award zone, not as a second trip.

On a one-way Aeroplan award, you're permitted to add a free stopover — meaning you can stay in an intermediate city for any length of time before continuing to your final destination. That 5,000-mile add-on is essentially the cost of a full additional destination. Compare that to booking a second one-way award from Istanbul to Bangkok, which would cost you another 40,000–55,000 Aeroplan points in business class. The math is decisive.

The routing must be geographically sensible — you can't fly backwards across the globe — but Aeroplan's allowance for multi-segment itineraries through Star Alliance hubs gives you enormous flexibility. Istanbul (IST) is a Turkish Airlines hub. Bangkok (BKK) is served by Thai Airways and several Star Alliance carriers. Both are Star Alliance partners. Both are bookable through Aeroplan at fixed chart rates with no fuel surcharges.

It has been revealed that the best part for the ChooseFI community is how accessible the underlying points are. Aeroplan accepts transfers from four major programs:.

In a recent development, chase's instant transfer speed is particularly valuable here. When you find business class availability — which can disappear quickly — you want to move points immediately. Having Chase Ultimate Rewards as your primary earning currency means you can search, find space, and transfer points before the availability window closes. The 1:1 ratio across all four programs means no conversion math — every point you earn translates directly to one Aeroplan mile.

Industry observers note that booking an Aeroplan stopover award in business class is genuinely one of the more complex redemptions in the travel rewards world, but it becomes manageable when you break it into distinct phases. Here's exactly how to do it.

Industry observers note that start by deciding on your two destinations. Aeroplan stopovers work best when your intermediate city is a major Star Alliance hub that lies geographically between your origin and final destination. Classic combinations include North America to Istanbul (Turkish Airlines hub) continuing to Southeast Asia, or North America to a European hub continuing to the Middle East or East Africa. Your stopover city should be somewhere you genuinely want to spend 2–5 days — this is a real trip, not just a layover.

According to recent reports, this is the most important and most time-consuming step. You need to find saver-level business class availability on both segments independently before you book.

According to recent reports, once you've confirmed availability on both segments, go to aeroplan.com and use the multi-city search function. Enter your full itinerary — origin, stopover city with your intended layover dates, and final destination.

Once you've confirmed the award is bookable and are ready to complete the reservation:.

Complete your booking on aeroplan.com or with a phone agent, confirm the stopover is properly reflected in your itinerary, and save every confirmation email. Verify your seats on each carrier's website immediately after booking.

Recent findings suggest that A stopover is an intentional break in your journey lasting more than 24 hours at a connecting city. Most airlines treat stopovers as separate tickets, charging full price for each segment. Aeroplan is one of the few programs that allows a free stopover on round-trip awards, letting you explore a connecting city for days before continuing to your final destination. This is fundamentally different from a layover, which is a brief connection of a few hours at an airport. The stopover must be in a city served by a Star Alliance carrier on your routing, and the key is that Aeroplan prices the entire itinerary as one award, not two.

The Route: Toronto (YYZ) → Istanbul (IST, 4-day stopover) → Bangkok (BKK) The Carrier: Turkish Airlines business class on both segments The Points Cost: 75,000 Aeroplan miles for the two segments + 5,000 miles for the stopover = 80,000 Aeroplan miles total Cash Equivalent: A comparable business class itinerary on this routing typically retails for $9,000–$12,000 in 2026, depending on when you search and how far in advance you book.

On the YYZ–IST segment — operated on a 787 or A330 — you'll have access to a lie-flat seat with direct aisle access, the Turkish Airlines Lounge in Istanbul (widely considered one of the best airport lounges in the world, full stop), and a meal service that reflects the airline's culinary reputation. The IST lounge alone — with its restaurant, spa, golf simulator, and sleeping areas — is worth lingering in even before your onward connection.

The IST–BKK segment puts you into Bangkok in the evening, ready for Thailand's extraordinary food, culture, and cost of living — which, for the FI-minded traveler, means your lodging and meals on the ground are remarkably affordable, stretching the value of your trip even further.

Total points cost for two lie-flat business class segments and a full European city stay: 80,000 miles, earned on everyday credit card spending. That's the entire proposition, and those numbers are real.

Call Aeroplan for complex routings. The online multi-city tool is functional but can struggle with nuanced stopover configurations. Phone agents are experienced with these bookings and have the same access to inventory. The call is worth it for an $80,000-point booking.

Industry observers note that leverage the open-jaw rule too. Aeroplan also allows open-jaw routing — fly into one city, depart from another. Combined with the stopover, you can design a route that visits three geographic points on a single award: fly into Istanbul, take trains or ferries to Athens, and fly home from Athens. The award prices the same way.

Don't assume partner availability matches Aeroplan's search. Turkish Airlines and other Star Alliance partners don't always make every seat available through Aeroplan's online portal. Don't book inflexible connecting flights. Long-haul itineraries with tight connections are a risk. Build in at least a 3-hour connection at hub airports to protect against irregular operations that could affect your award segments.

This redemption is purpose-built for the advanced travel rewards enthusiast in the ChooseFI community — someone who has already mastered the basics (earning transferable points, understanding award charts, booking straightforward partner awards) and is ready to unlock the next level of value.

Recent findings suggest that are you trying to win the Mega Millions, but your numbers never seem to come up? It may be time to look for better ways to make money. Fortunately, you can earn extra cash without going and getting a “real job.”.

It has been revealed that what are the best ways to avoid sitting in a cubicle all day? Some money-making strategies require an upfront investment, while others let you earn money in your free time with the help of apps.

Read on to learn the best ways to earn cash without a regular 9-5 job, plus tips on how almost anyone can get started.

Recent findings suggest that one of the easiest ways to earn money is by signing up to participate in market research studies. You won’t make much, a few dollars here and there, but you can create a free account and get started within minutes.

You’ll be paid in PayPal cash or gift cards for sharing your opinion and completing other tasks online.

Sources indicate that E-Poll Market Research is one of the top companies to consider for this type of work. They make it easy to create an account and answer survey questions.

However, there are plenty of other options to consider, including:.

While market research gigs won’t make you rich, it’s something you can do during your spare time.

Industry observers note that if you have a book idea, turning your story into an eBook can help you earn passive income without a regular job. Kindle Direct Publishing can even help you format your book for Kindle, at which point you can market and sell your book to millions of potential readers who shop on Amazon.com.

How much can you earn writing eBooks? That depends on how many books you write, how much you sell them for, and how successful you are at marketing your book. Selling 20 books per month with a profit of $7 per book would net you $140 per month and $1,680 per year.

Meanwhile, selling 100 books per month at $7 per book would net you $700 per month and $8,400 per year. Need a little inspiration? Here’s an article that highlights you how to make your first $1,000 selling eBooks.

Recent findings suggest that you can earn a lot of money by starting a blog or niche website and monetizing it. I should know. I started Good Financial Cents more than a decade ago, and have earned millions of dollars through the monetization of this site since its earliest days.

How do you make money blogging? Earning real income with a website isn’t as easy as it looks, but there are plenty of monetization strategies you can try.

Here are the most common ways blogs make money:.

If you’re curious about what it takes to earn money blogging, consider signing up for my Make 1K Challenge. It’s free and can help you earn your first $1,000 online with some of the blog monetization strategies I’ve already mentioned.

You could argue that freelance work is like a regular job, but working at home and on your terms is much different from traditional employment. The fact is, most freelancers are fully remote – they can work from anywhere in the world with a laptop and an internet connection.

Plus, they can hire and fire clients based on their personal needs and preferences, and their income potential is unlimited. According to ZipRecruiter, freelancers in the U.S. average $63.53 per hour.

Sources indicate that of course, you’ll need a marketable skill to find paid work as a freelancer. This could be freelance writing, design skills, marketing expertise, or something else.

You can use several websites to market your skills as a freelancer, including:.

It has been revealed that healthyWage makes it possible to earn money while you lose weight. You won’t earn a ton of cash through the app, but you can earn a few dollars and use it to supplement other income you have.

The more weight you lose, the more money you can make. For example, the HealthyWage website claims some of their clients who lost more than 100 pounds managed to earn anywhere from $1,400 to $3,000.

However, the HW weight loss calculator shows potential earnings of $578 to $828 for people who only have 15 pounds to lose.

If you have a car you rarely use and want to earn some side income, you can consider renting it out with Turo, a ride-sharing platform that connects car owners with people who need a short-term rental. You can set your price, although you’ll have more success if you price your car competitively.

In a recent development, nicer vehicles in high-demand areas can easily fetch rates that surpass $100 per day through this platform. Turo notes that in-demand cars rented out regularly can bring in anywhere from $10,000 to $20,000 per year in net profit.

Plus, almost anyone can rent out their car provided it meets the guidelines of the Turo platform. Your car must be 12 years old or newer with less than 130,000 miles. It must be worth less than $200,000 (no Lambo’s), and you must also meet Turo’s auto insurance requirements.

Do you have a spare bedroom in your home that you never use? Maybe you have a basement or garage apartment you could fix up and begin renting for a profit?

In a recent development, either way, Airbnb lets you rent out rooms and other spaces in your home on any dates you prefer. You must let renters know they’re renting a room in a home vs. an entire apartment or house and provide as much additional detail as possible.

The amount you can earn will depend on where you live and the type of accommodation you can offer. However, expensive cities like Chicago, Newly introduced York, and San Francisco have plenty of rooms for rent that go for well over $100 per night.

You may not have an entire room you can rent, but even if you have some storage space, Neighbor.com allows you to rent it out to others in need.

Common spaces rented through this platform include.

According to recent reports, the Neighbor.com platform makes it easy to advertise your unused space so that people nearby can inquire if they’re interested. Also, note that the platform offers insurance that can protect you if some of your client’s items are damaged or stolen while in your care.

How much can you make renting out extra space? It depends on how much space you have to rent and where it’s located. However, Neighbor.com shows a range of rental space options that cost anywhere from $20 to $100+ per month.

Industry observers note that investing in dividend stocks is one of the best ways to earn money without a regular job. Many early retirees find a way to live and pay bills based solely on the dividends they receive from various stocks.

According to recent reports, but what exactly is a dividend stock? For the most part, they are regular stocks but with a track record of sharing their profits with investors through dividends.

Dividends can also be earned in exchange-traded funds (ETFs) or mutual funds, and they can be significant once you build up a large portfolio.

Since dividends are paid by profitable companies, they tend to be seen as less risky for investors. If you’re curious about what it takes to get started with this strategy, this post explains how to invest in dividend stocks.

Housesitting is an option if you’re somewhat mobile and can move from place to place. Generally, you can find house-sitting gigs through word of mouth, referrals, or online portals like Craigslist.org or Facebook Marketplace.

That remarked, not all house-sitting gigs are paid. Some offer the potential for exotic travel instead and free lodging for a week to several months.

Recent findings suggest that either way, a website called TrustedHousesitters is the best place to find house-sitting gigs. Some jobs posted are for house-sitting only, while others require house sitters to provide basic care for pets or plants.

Sources indicate that if you have serious wanderlust and want to travel far and wide, this platform can help make it happen. Many gigs posted online are in countries like Australia, Ireland, France, and Switzerland.

If you love animals and want to earn money taking care of them, several platforms can help turn your dream into a reality.

Recent findings suggest that for example, Rover.com lets you provide basic care for dogs or cats in your home, or you can pick up dog walking gigs. Another mobile app, called Wag!, lets you do more of the same.

Sources indicate that you can set your rates for all types of work through these platforms, and your availability. While earnings vary by location and job, most people watch dogs and cats for anywhere from $40 to $100 per night.

Real estate investing may seem like a pipe dream if you hope to earn income without a job but hear me out. There are many ways to earn income through real estate without owning physical property or dealing with the hassles of being a landlord.

In a recent development, you can invest in real estate investment trusts (REITs) that let you build wealth over time. You can also use a platform called Fundrise to invest in real estate with a minimum investment of $10.

Fundrise lets you purchase eREITs, large investment funds that acquire, own, or operate multi-residential and commercial properties. The income you earn is entirely passive since it handles the work of finding income-producing properties and managing them.

While returns are never guaranteed, Fundrise investors have achieved very solid returns. Investors who use the platform earned an average return of 7.31% in 2020, followed by 22.99% in 2021, 1.50% in 2022 and -7.45% in 2023 (their first down year).

You can earn income on your spare change by investing it using Acorns. The roundup savings app syncs to your debit or credit card rounds up every purchase you make to the nearest dollar, and invests the difference. Once it’s set up, there’s no work on your part.

Most of the money is invested in ETFs and managed by the world’s top investment firms like Vanguard and BlackRock. While this app makes it easy to invest small amounts of money, it’s not free to use. Personal plans start at $3 per month, while a family plan costs just $5.

If you’re looking for some paid gigs that are relatively easy, consider setting up a profile on TaskRabbit, an online platform that lets you get paid for completing various tasks, such as:.

Sources indicate that projects typically pay between $30 and $100, although some pay significantly more than that. TaskRabbit also lets you pick and choose the jobs you want to take on based on your availability so that you can work entirely on your schedule.

If you love taking photographs and have a knack for getting professional-looking images, you can use your skills and expertise to sell photos online.

Websites like Depositphotos and iStockPhoto pay photographers to supply them with stock photos they can sell to writers, publications, and various online platforms.

The best part about this side hustle is that you can get started with the equipment you already have. While you can use a professional camera if you want to, many smartphones take professional-quality photos.

Earning a bank bonus is another way to earn money without a regular job, but you’ll need an upfront investment to get started. Most bonus offers require you to deposit a specific amount of money and keep it in your account for up to 12 months.

You may also be required to set up direct deposit to earn a bank bonus, and other terms and conditions may apply.

Where can you find the best bank bonuses? While bonus offers constantly change, you can start by checking with banks like Chase, HSBC, Radius Bank, and Wells Fargo.

Flipping furniture requires some upfront legwork and potentially even some artistic talent, but you can earn a solid income with this strategy if you know what you’re doing.

Essentially, this side hustle requires you to shop at thrift stores, garage sales, and online platforms to find furniture that will ultimately sell for more than you paid.

From there, you can sell the furniture as-is or clean it up and paint it with the goal of fetching an even higher price.

You can make money driving for Uber or Lyft on your own time, picking and choosing the days and hours you want to work.

Not only is rideshare work one of the most flexible side hustles, but you can earn $20 per hour and more with tips.

If you are low on free time but still want to make money without a job, consider selling stuff you don’t need. An array of online platforms makes it a breeze, although some platforms work better for selling.

For example, you can use Poshmark to earn money selling used clothing and accessories, while used electronics tend to sell best on platforms like eBay.com, Decluttr, BuyBackWorld, and Gazelle.

If you have home decor, furniture, or workout equipment to sell, you’ll almost always do better unloading those items locally on Facebook Marketplace.

Starting a YouTube channel is another way to earn money without a job, but that doesn’t mean it’s not work. The fact is, that creating quality videos and building an audience takes a lot of creativity and time. Plus, not everyone who tries to build a YouTube channel will succeed.

According to recent reports, that said, you can earn income without a regular job. I know because I have done it with my YouTube channel, Wealth Hacker.

How much you can earn on YouTube varies quite a bit, but it’s possible to earn thousands of dollars per month. If you’re curious about monetizing videos, my in-depth guide will show you how to make money on YouTube.

Donating plasma is a unique way to earn money without a job, although it’s not very glamorous. DonatingPlasma.org makes it easy to find plasma donation centers in your area, and you can earn as much as $100 for your first donation.

Sources indicate that that said, subsequent plasma donations typically earn closer to $50. You’ll also be limited by the number of times you can donate plasma within a month. However, it’s possible to use this side gig to earn an extra $500 per month, which you can use to supplement your primary income.

If you are willing to complete various tasks that help regular workers do their jobs, consider becoming a crowd worker. This gig will have you finishing up to-do lists of jobs that don’t require specific technical skills.

For example, you may get paid to proofread documents, label images, upgrade a resume, complete a form, or complete a data entry assignment.

Several platforms help you find crowd-working gigs, but the best ones include Microworkers and Clickworker.

According to recent reports, if you want to do something simple that will get you moving, consider delivering groceries using apps like Instacart or Shipt. You get paid hourly, plus tips and all you have to do is head to the store, purchase groceries according to a list, and deliver them to people in your neighborhood.

The gig is extremely flexible, similar to driving for Uber or Lyft.

It has been revealed that another non-job gig lets you get paid to deliver packages for Amazon.com. You can do this through a platform called Amazon Flex, which promises its drivers anywhere from $18 to $25 per hour.

It has been revealed that unlike a regular Amazon job, Flex lets you pick the day and the hours you want to work. To get started, you need to create a free account, get approved, and start reserving blocks of time you want to deliver packages.

It has been revealed that finally, you can earn money by selling unwanted or unused gift cards in your possession. This hustle is made easy thanks to platforms like GiftDeals.com and CardCash.com.

According to recent reports, you won’t get the total value of your gift cards, but you should get 90% or more of the gift card balance for each card you sell. While selling gift cards for less than their total value may not seem ideal, it’s better than not using them and getting nothing in return.

According to recent reports, finally, you can earn small amounts of money by signing up with the best online survey sites. Not only is this side hustle as easy as it gets, but you can participate and get paid during your spare time and even on your phone.

Other online survey sites to check out include the following:.

There you have it, 26 ways to make money without a job. While many of the jobs on our list won’t replace your 9-5, they can be a great way to increase your income so you can pay off debt or break the cycle of living paycheck to paycheck.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that open a GoFundMe Giving Fund if you itemize and strategy to give cash, stocks, or exchange-traded funds over a few years, since it charges no administrative fee and lets you contribute or grant as little as $5. Skip it for crypto or private organization shares, and give straight to charities instead if you take the standard deduction.

GoFundMe Giving Funds is a donor-advised fund for givers who want a tax deduction now and time to choose charities later, run since June 2025 by GoFundMe Giving Fund, a 501(c)(3) public charity separate from GoFundMe. It charges no administrative fee, where DAFgiving360 charges 0.60% a year on the first $500,000, which works out to $60 a year on a $10,000 balance.

According to recent reports, itemizers who give cash, stocks, or ETFs over a few years lose none of their balance to an administrative fee here. If you take the standard deduction, give straight to charities instead, because starting in 2026 up to $1,000 of cash gifts ($2,000 on a joint return) is deductible without itemizing, and contributions to a donor-advised fund don’t qualify.

Learn more about GoFundMe Giving Funds.

#56459. How Unlimited Free Stuff from Amazon Almost Ruined My Retirement

📅 07 Oct 2025 • ⏱️ 10m • 📚 Deep Dive (2048 w)

How Unlimited Free Stuff from Amazon Almost Ruined My Retirement

📅 07 Oct 2025 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2048 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Mrmoneymustache

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It all started last winter when I innocently posted a review for a heated vest I had bought on Amazon.
  • You’ve been selected to join Amazon Vine for writing helpful reviews!”.
  • I was already aware of Amazon Vine since I had seen product reviews from other people in the program – typically called “Vine Voices.” The basic idea of this program is that you can order stuff from Amazon for free, as long as you agree to review at least 80% of the things you order.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It all started last winter when I innocently posted a review for a heated vest I had bought on Amazon. I was happy with this fun fresh way to beat the winter and wanted to share it with others, so I gave it five stars. But soon after I clicked “Submit”, I got an email from Amazon which said something like,.

“Congratulations! You’ve been selected to join Amazon Vine for writing helpful reviews!”.

I was already aware of Amazon Vine since I had seen product reviews from other people in the program – typically called “Vine Voices.” The basic idea of this program is that you can order stuff from Amazon for free, as long as you agree to review at least 80% of the things you order.

“Hey, that’s cool”, I thought, “Who doesn’t like free stuff?

Especially since I’ve already been writing product reviews out of the goodness of my heart – why not be rewarded for it?”.

So without giving it much further thought, I clicked “accept” on their terms and conditions and joined the program.

And so began a saga that has taken me on a surprising journey over the past nine months causing me to:.

Okay, I’ll admit that there were also some upsides. My original idea was partly to save some money, by getting stuff I genuinely would have bought anyway, in a way that sounded fun. And that did happen – I saved at least a few thousand dollars on tools and materials for my construction business and the MMM-HQ Coworking space, for free. Plus, at least some of the motivation for signing up was to put myself through an experiment so I could write this blog article about it. And if you’re reading this, it looks like that happened too.

But I was still surprised at how powerful the combination of small nudges and incentives from Amazon was able to hijack my frugality instincts –  and get me to do a bunch of work that wasn’t really the best use of my time.

Recent findings suggest that so I figured if we review my journey and break it down with a bit of Behavioral Science, we could all learn a few valuable things by laughing at Mr. Money Mustache’s folly.

Scarcity Brain and the Online Casino Effect.

One of the most interesting books I’ve read in recent years is Michael Easter’s Scarcity Brain. It’s an exploration of the sneaky ways that modern gambling platforms, marketing and social media algorithms are all built upon two weaknesses in our evolutionary programming:.

As I look back now, I realize that I fell straight into those same traps, because the Vine program has all the key properties of a casino or a TikTok feed:.

In a recent development, but occasionally, there will be genuinely useful things like super nice light fixtures, tools and plumbing parts, an EV charger, and even some clothing. My favorite ridiculous Eagle shirt as featured in the Mustachianism music video was an Amazon Vine find.

As were a whole supply of super-realistic artificial plants, which while tacky in principle, have been amazing for hard-to-water courtyard garden areas at the MMM HQ.

It has been revealed that I also had a lot of fun roping in friends and coworkers from HQ to help and share in the bounty. I let them help me request and review stuff that they wanted, and then they got to keep it. This seemed like a win/win because we shared the work and the fun of laughing at some of the ridiculous products available.

Still, as I went through this experiment this spring and summer and allowed the system to coax me into doing 80 reviews so I could upgrade my account from Vine Silver to Vine Gold*, I noticed something didn’t feel quite right.

In a recent development, I was checking the Vine page every day for scores, even when I didn’t actually need anything. It would usually be a bust, but just often enough, something I actually wanted would come up, and I’d order it before it was too late. Scarcity and unpredictable rewards at work.

It has been revealed that then the bounty would come, I’d unpack it and photograph it with assembly-line speed so I could batch-write all the reviews once per week or so. For every review I did, I was spending time I’d rather spend doing something else. And for every questionable item I got, I was creating pollution and trash from its manufacturing and packaging – directly contradicting the main values of my life and my reason for writing this blog. And I saw all of this, yet I kept doing it!

So Was This The Downfall of MMM?

During the worst of this consumerism bender, things were dire. I was getting packages almost every day and my recycling bin was overflowing with cardboard. My son and my girlfriend started laughing at some of my more frivolous purchases, so I found myself discreetly tucking away the boxes when they were around to evade scrutiny.

Recent findings suggest that but eventually, I moved into a recovery stage. I had been letting this habit continue out of laziness and as a form of procrastination: it’s very easy to order shit online and pretend I’m doing something useful, and much more difficult to get moving to do the things that really make my life enjoyable.

But I’m old enough to know that hitting the running trails and the gym for my daily workouts, and making progress on all my construction projects, and focusing on the computer as a creative tool rather than an entertainment device so I can get stuff done like this blog post, are the things that bring me the most joy.

Industry observers note that admittedly, some of the sucky factors of the Vine program helped make it easier to recover too. For every genuinely useful thing I found like a contractor-grade extension cord, I had to scan through endless screens of trinkets which not only wasted my time but actually pissed me off at their very existence.

Recent findings suggest that I also noticed some of the deliberately reviewer-unfriendly features built into the program which reminded me that we reviewers are definitely just low-wage workers rather than any form of VIP. The search functionality is crap, and there is no way to filter or sort the results, because they want you to have to look through everything and they don’t care about the value of your time.

Then there is the hilariously bureaucratic AI-based evaluation system which would occasionally flag my totally tame, factual reviews as “Not meeting our Community Standards” without explaining what the problem was. So I’d have to go in and edit my review, randomly changing a couple of words and maybe some punctuation, and suddenly the AI would be pacified and accept my review. Just dumb.

This is What “Fuck You Money” is For!

Recent findings suggest that it dawned on me that for many people, this is just what “work” looks like. You are given a bunch of tasks and a bunch of rules to follow, in a system you didn’t create and don’t get much say in changing. And then as long as you crank out your TPS Reports without rocking the boat too much, you get your paycheck.

It reminded me of the Uber Driving experiment I did way back in 2017: as soon as I started working as a driver, I could immediately see dozens of improvements that could be made to the system that would make it function better for both drivers and passengers. But since I wasn’t the boss, nobody wanted to hear my ideas.

Experiences like these remind me that while I love hard work and I love learning newly introduced things every day, I greatly prefer being the boss. And I’ve gotten pretty damned accustomed to it after 20 years of financial independence, so I see no need to give it up.

According to recent reports, one interesting “gotcha” of the Vine program is that they do keep track of all the free stuff you get and send you a 1099 for its retail value at the end of the year. So it’s not really free, just discounted to whatever your marginal tax rate is (about 25% for me this year). If we peek into my account right now, this is how my 2025 is looking:.

So I got about $7000 worth of stuff, and could owe up to $1750 of tax on it. In my case, about 75% of it was “sold” to my business for commercial use (construction supplies which I used on jobs or HQ renovations) so it was effectively converted into real income rather than just tax burden. Some of it was stuff I would have bought anyway for my own house which I’ll gladly pay the taxes on. But there is also probably about $1000 of pure nonsense in there as well, for which I’ll owe a tax bill of $250 as penance for my itchy trigger finger on that “Order” button.

Thanks to some advice from wise readers in the comments (below), I have since learned that in most cases you can mark down this estimated value by 80% before declaring it – because you have effectively eliminated most of the resale value by opening and reviewing the product. Thus my tax bill will be more like $50 rather than $250. More detail in this Reddit discussion here.

In a recent development, so here we are today. While I admit that I didn’t explicitly cancel my account, I used the “Keystone Habit” trick to override the temptation to view the Vine page – mapping that browser bookmark to my daily habits list instead, a little chart which I call my “Badassity Tracker”. The net result is that every time I click it, I’m taken straight to a reminder to get up from the computer and do a quick round of exercise, so I do that instead.

Industry observers note that and of course my writing of this article may be a violation of the terms and conditions of the program (“the first rule of Vine is to not talk about Vine”), so it might even get canceled on me. (and if so I’ll let you know because that would be funny story as well).

But I learned a lot about habits and addiction, and realized that this same feeling might be what drives people into One More Year Syndrome, as they keep working even when they can afford to quit. I have now coached enough people through this situation to see it is way more common than I would have ever guessed.

Industry observers note that as with all MMM articles, there’s a real life lesson in this story. It’s not really about Vine or me or my habits, it’s about you continuing to look at yourself and your life, and always questioning your own assumptions or patterns. And asking the people you trust most for feedback as well:.

Industry observers note that we will never be perfect, but the great news is we don’t have to be. All it takes is a little bit of self reflection and putting ourselves on a slightly better path, as often as we can as life goes on. We are all on a very long journey, so even a tiny course correction can make a huge difference in where we end up.

Open Bright Start 529 if you pay Illinois income tax, since you can deduct contributions on your state return, or if choosing it costs you no home-state tax break. Its index portfolios charge 0.09% a year or less. If your state’s break requires its own blueprint, fund that plan first.

Bright Start is Illinois’s 529 plan for savers who invest without an advisor, open to residents of every state, and its age-based portfolios shift from stocks toward bonds and cash as a child nears college. At a 6% yearly return before fees, a family saving $200 a month for 18 years pays about $500 in fees in the index versions by our math, against about $2,400 at Morningstar’s 0.43% average for age-based portfolios in 2025.

Illinois families should start here, since they get a state deduction on top of index fees about a fifth of the 0.43% average, and so should savers who lose no home-state tax break by choosing it. Savers whose state gives its 529 deduction or credit only for its own strategy should open that plan first, since that break is a sure saving each year they contribute.

Tech Report: Build a Free Home Workout Proposal – Two Strength Days and 150 Minutes of Cardio

💡 Key Takeaways
  • A home workout plan needs no trainer or paid app.
  • It has been revealed that the 150 minutes and the two strength days come from the Department of Health and Human Services’ Physical Activity Guidelines for Americans.
  • Sources indicate that A walk counts as brisk at 2.5 miles per hour or faster, and 75 minutes of vigorous activity like running meets the cardio target on its own.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A home workout plan needs no trainer or paid app. Federal exercise guidelines call for at least 150 minutes of brisk walking or other moderate cardio a week, plus strength work on two or more days. Put each session on your calendar, train with body weight and household items, and add reps or minutes every week or two.

It has been revealed that the 150 minutes and the two strength days come from the Department of Health and Human Services’ Physical Activity Guidelines for Americans. They tell you how much exercise is enough, which is part of what a trainer or a paid app charges for.

Sources indicate that A walk counts as brisk at 2.5 miles per hour or faster, and 75 minutes of vigorous activity like running meets the cardio target on its own. For strength work, the guidelines say to do each move until one more repetition would be hard, and a single set of 8 to 12 repetitions per move is effective.

Five moves cover every major muscle group: squats and lunges for your legs and hips, push-ups for your chest, shoulders, and arms, rows for your back, and a plank for your core. Do push-ups against a kitchen counter until you can do 8 from the floor. For rows, bend forward and pull a gallon jug of water or a backpack loaded with books toward your ribs, and wear the backpack for squats once body-weight squats feel easy.

For cardio, pick what you’ll keep doing, whether that’s brisk walks, runs, or a free workout video. Then give every session a day and a time, as you would an appointment. A 40-year-old could do 25-minute strength sessions on Monday, Wednesday, and Friday and 50-minute brisk walks on Tuesday, Thursday, and Saturday. That’s 150 minutes of cardio and three strength days, with Sunday off, at no cost.

In a recent development, write down the repetitions for each move and the minutes of each cardio session, in a notebook, a free app, or the printable initiative from the federal Move Your Way activity planner. Every week or two, add two repetitions, a second set, more weight in the backpack, or five minutes of cardio, since the guidelines call for raising activity gradually over weeks to months.

If you’ve been inactive, start smaller, with 10-minute walks and one strength day a week, and build to the full plan over several weeks.

Amelia Earhart Search Find Trees, Not Plane. Mystery Remains

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A highly anticipated expedition to solve one of aviation’s greatest mysteries has concluded without finding the wreckage of Amelia Earhart’s missing plane.
  • A 17-person team from the Archaeological Legacy Institute and Purdue University recently returned from Nikumaroro, a remote and uninhabited atoll in the Pacific Ocean.
  • Their primary objective was to investigate the Taraia Object, a mysterious shape in a shallow lagoon that researchers first noticed in 2020 on satellite and historical aerial photos.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A highly anticipated expedition to solve one of aviation’s greatest mysteries has concluded without finding the wreckage of Amelia Earhart’s missing plane.

A 17-person team from the Archaeological Legacy Institute and Purdue University recently returned from Nikumaroro, a remote and uninhabited atoll in the Pacific Ocean.

Their primary objective was to investigate the Taraia Object, a mysterious shape in a shallow lagoon that researchers first noticed in 2020 on satellite and historical aerial photos. While some hoped the anomaly was the remnants of Earhart’s Lockheed Electra, the expedition determined it was entirely natural.

Recent findings suggest that the Taraia Object on a satellite image. Located at Nikumaroro. Photo: Archaeological Legacy Institute.

Recent findings suggest that according to Purdue University officials, the object was a cluster of large fallen trees resting on a sandbar. Much of the debris observed in satellite images had already broken up and washed away, leaving a single Y-shaped piece. The reflective, metallic glint seen from above turned out to be a hardened layer of coral sand coating the wood.

According to recent reports, on the way to the atoll. Photo: Purdue Research Foundation.

In a recent development, the five-day operation proved logistically complicated. Workers faced dense brush and a large population of giant coconut crabs. The nocturnal activities of the massive crabs forced the crew to abandon plans to camp on the atoll and to return to the ship each evening. During the day, the crabs simply minded their own business.

One of the crew holds a coconut crab. Photo: Purdue Research Foundation.

Despite the difficulties, researchers recovered a few minor artifacts to study lagoon drift patterns, including a 76cm steel tube.

The team emphasized that ruling out the Taraia Object does not disprove the broader “castaway hypothesis.” For decades, historians have investigated the theory that Earhart and navigator Fred Noonan drifted off course during their 1937 global circumnavigation attempt, landing on Nikumaroro’s reef after failing to find Howland Island.

Amelia Earhart. Photo: amelia.prf.org.

Purdue University, where Earhart once served as a career counselor and aviation advisor, stated that its commitment to the search remains unchanged.

“Amelia Earhart never gave up — she kept pushing boundaries and flying into the unknown,” said Steve Schultz, Purdue’s general counsel and field assistant, after the expedition. “She kept flying, and we will keep searching.”.

For more details, extensive project documentation, and a gallery of expedition photographs, you can visit the official mission site at Amelia.prf.org.

From left to right: Steve Schultz, Sirisha Bandla, and Marc Hagle, members of the research team. Photo: Purdue Research Foundation.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Jost Kobusch is back in Nepal, preparing for the fourth round of his Everest project.
  • “If I am good at something, it’s planning,” the 34-year-old German told ExplorersWeb.
  • Sources indicate that kobusch arrived in Kathmandu two weeks ago, together with friends Nicolas Scheidtweiler, Manuela Brummer, and photographer Alex Pichon.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Jost Kobusch is back in Nepal, preparing for the fourth round of his Everest project. His long-term goal is to climb solo in winter, without oxygen, self-supported, and via the Lho La and the West Ridge.

“If I am good at something, it’s planning,” the 34-year-old German told ExplorersWeb. In this case, his plan is to arrive at the mountain in the best shape possible, physically and mentally.

Sources indicate that kobusch arrived in Kathmandu two weeks ago, together with friends Nicolas Scheidtweiler, Manuela Brummer, and photographer Alex Pichon. The group soon moved to Manang in the Annapurna region and began acclimatizing in the Chulu range.

Industry observers note that jost Kobusch (in yellow) scouts around Manang. Photo: Alex Pichon.

The blueprint was to spend a few nights at altitude and traverse the four Chulu peaks, all above 6,000m. “[However,] expeditions rarely unfold exactly as expected,” Kobusch admitted.

According to recent reports, A member in the team felt exhausted after reaching the summit of the second peak, and the group abandoned the traverse there. “At least, we traversed from the summit of Chulu Far East (6,059m) to the top of Chulu East (6,444m) from the southeast,” Kobusch remarked. He says their line between the two peaks was fresh.

In a recent development, the line followed by Kobusch and his team up Chulu East. Photo: Alex Pichon.

Sources indicate that their next blueprint will be to climb a 7,000m peak in the area before Kobusch moves to the Khumbu in November. “I want to reach 8,000m, but on a different mountain than Everest, before the beginning of winter,” he mentioned.

He wants to be completely acclimatized by the time he starts working on Everest on December 22, the start of calendar winter. Kobusch will have two photographers in Base Camp, but he will climb alone.

Acclimatization in Manang, Photo: Alex Pichon.

“I need to be able to move efficiently, make good decisions when I’m tired, manage risk alone, and stay comfortable in an environment where very small mistakes can have very serious consequences,” Kobusch recently wrote on social media. He states that so far, all is going well. “I’m feeling good, I’ve done my homework, and I will start again on Everest better prepared than ever.”.

Kobusch has attempted winter Everest solo on three previous occasions, always via the Lho La and the West Ridge, thus avoiding venturing alone into the Khumbu Icefall.

In his first attempt in 2019-20, he reached the West Shoulder and pushed above 7,300m. On the second attempt in 2021-22, high winds didn’t let him go beyond 6,400m. He planned to try again the following year, but he caught dengue fever while training in Nepal and had to cancel.

Sources indicate that once recovered, he soloed Denali in February-March 2023. Everest had to wait one more year, this time due to a back injury. On the third attempt in 2024-25, he reached his highest point yet: 7,537m on December 27.

Kobusch’s highest point is shown with a green circle, and the Hornbein Couloir is the pink line on the 3D map by RealityMaps.

According to recent reports, “The chances of success are not particularly high,” he recently wrote. “If I had to put a number on it, I would say around 20%. But that does not make the attempt meaningless. If anything, it is part of what makes it interesting.”.

Having more than one type of debt is common, and that’s especially true once you graduate from college and start your first “real job.” You may have credit card debt, an auto loan, and a mortgage payment to make once you buy your first home. It’s also common to have other random debts to cover, including student loans.

It has been revealed that if you’re like many who took out loans during college, you will likely be paying them off after you graduate. In fact, 82% of students who borrowed loans expect to be making payments post-graduation, according to a recent College Ave Student Loans survey.

That said, you’ll want to make sure you’re balancing debt repayment with your savings goals along the way.

Recent findings suggest that you’ll also want to make sure you’re paying down debts in the optimal order, or in a way that will help you save the most money on interest as possible while aligning with your goals. Which debts should you pay off first? Here’s a rundown of how to get the best results:.

No matter which types of debt you have, credit card debt should be your first priority. Why? Because credit card debt is likely the most expensive debt you have by far.

Federal Reserve data demonstrates the average credit card interest rate on accounts assessed interest came in at around 22% as of May 2023, yet your credit card could easily be charging higher rates than the average.

To save as much money as possible, you should strive to pay as much as you can toward high-interest credit card bills each month. You can also pay down credit card debt faster with the help of a debt consolidation loan or a 0% APR balance transfer credit card.

It has been revealed that other unsecured debts like personal loan debt should come next in the debt payoff pecking order. After all, unsecured debts tend to have higher interest rates than secured debts like auto loans. In fact, the Federal Reserve also reported that the average interest rate on a 24-month personal loan came in at 11.48% as of May 2023, compared to the average rate of 7.81% on a 60-month auto loan.

Ideally, you’ll start paying more toward personal loan debt and other unsecured debts after all credit card debt is entirely paid off, although you should make at least the minimum payment on all your bills throughout the entire process.

It has been revealed that the next debt you’ll want to tackle is your student loans. I suggest focusing on these loans after other unsecured debts, since federal student loans (and many private student loans) come with low fixed interest rates and monthly payments that will not change over time. If you have federal student loans, you may even want to look into income-driven repayment intends.

If you’re hoping to pay down student loans faster or just want to save money on interest, you can also consider refinancing your student loans to get a shorter repayment timeline, a lower monthly payment, or both. Just remember that refinancing federal student loans can mean losing access to income-driven repayment plans and federal protections like deferment and forbearance.

It has been revealed that once you have paid off or substantially paid down all your other debts, you can focus your efforts on secured debts you have like mortgage loans and auto loans. These debts should be dealt with last since they are secured with collateral and tend to offer lower interest rates as a result. For example, you can consider paying more than the minimum on your mortgage, a car loan, or both until they’re paid off completely.

Then again, you may want to pay off debts with extremely low interest rates as slowly as possible to free up more cash flow for living expenses and investments. If you took out a mortgage in January of 2021 when the average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed rate home loan was as low as 2.65%, for example, it makes sense to make the minimum payment on that debt and invest your extra cash instead.

Recent findings suggest that it’s notable to make sure you balance debt repayment with other financial considerations. After all, focusing too much on debt repayment early in life can leave you behind when it comes to investing for retirement or saving up for a first home.

While you’ll want to eliminate credit card debt and other high-interest debts as rapidly as you can, even if you have to stop saving and investing for a while, you can pay down student loan debt and secured debts at a slower pace while saving and investing for the future along the way.

Sources indicate that finally, make sure you have adequate emergency savings throughout your entire debt payoff journey, or that you begin saving for emergencies as soon as you can. Without a fully funded emergency fund, you can end up relying on credit cards and other loans to get by and ruin your debt payoff progress in the process.

It has been revealed that how much should you save? While most experts recommend having an emergency fund that can cover three to six months of expenses, it’s okay to start small if you have to.

In a recent development, having more than one type of debt is how it works for most people, especially when you’re young and in the early stages of your career. When it comes to paying it off, however, you’ll want to make sure you have a concrete blueprint that can help you reduce interest charges and get where you want to be.

Industry observers note that focusing on credit card debt and other unsecured debts first always makes sense, since these debts aren’t secured by an asset and tend to charge much higher interest rates. You can focus on student loans next, followed by other secured debts you have like a home loan or car loan.

It has been revealed that in the meantime, make sure you have an adequate emergency fund and invest in it for retirement. After all, debt won’t last forever if you’re serious about repayment, and saving and investing early can help you benefit from compound interest and avoid using credit cards for surprise expenses. Creating a budget to track these factors is your best bet.

If you need help creating one, or simply don’t know where to start, use this budget worksheet as your guide – you’ll reach financial freedom in no time.

If fear keeps you from starting a business, make the worst case small enough to live with. Start on the side while you keep your job, and before you spend anything, set a budget you can afford to lose and a date to decide whether it’s working. Spend more only once customers are paying.

Plenty of owners already run a business alongside another job. Nearly four in five U.S. small businesses have no employees, a 2026 Federal Reserve report found, and for almost four in 10 of those, the business isn’t the main owner’s only job.

According to recent reports, you don’t need a brand-upcoming idea either. A better or more local version of something people already buy is enough. A service you know how to do can start with a laptop, a simple website, and some software. On the side, it takes only the hours you give it. And if you sell under your own legal name, you don’t have to register the business anywhere, the Small Business Administration says, though you’ll still need any license or permit your work requires before your first sale.

Keeping your job also improves the business’s odds. In a study published in the Academy of Management Journal, people who started a business while still employed and went full time later were 33% less likely to fail than those who quit a job to start one.

Before you spend anything, set three limits:.

Industry observers note that picture a bookkeeper who caps her costs at $500 for software and a website, then does the books for three local shops on weekends. After a year, the clients pay enough that she cuts her job to part time.

Industry observers note that expect mistakes, like a price set too low or a client who pays late. On a small budget each one costs little, so fix it swiftly instead of trying to prevent every one.

Write the three limits down today, before you buy anything for the business.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The three-man Russian team returned to Everest’s West Ridge but found the route even more difficult than they expected. After two days of struggle, they’re heading back to Base Camp.

On October 20, Andrei Vasiliev, Serguey Kondrashkin, and Vitaly Shipilov went back up to the Lho La and pitched their tent on the wide plateau beyond. They still had time to fix more rope higher up.

“We moved…over terrain we’d already covered on the previous rotation,” the climbers texted to team member Natalya Belyankina, who had to abandon the expedition due to illness.

In a recent development, “The weather is good: sunny, with light winds, but cold,” they noted. “Progress was painfully slow today due to heavy packs and a persistent cough,” the climbers noted later.

Industry observers note that on Wednesday, they hoped to reach 7,500m, spend the night there, check the route ahead, and then retreat to the plateau. However, they didn’t get as far as they had planned.

Recent findings suggest that “We didn’t cover much ground today,” leader Andrei Vsiliev texted Anna Piunova of The Mountain Club. “The route is no walk in the park. We have to climb steep snowy slopes that conceal rock sections underneath.”.

To make things worse, they found no suitable bivy spots at their highest point, so they had to retreat to a place where they could pitch their tent for the night. Today, they were just too exhausted to keep going.

Recent findings suggest that “We’re heading down; we’re sick and need to recover,” Vasiliev told Belyankina. “We can barely keep moving.”.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that on-time phone and utility payments rarely reach your credit report, so they don’t help your score. Link the bank account you pay them from to Experian Boost, a free tool that adds them to your Experian report. It’s most worth doing when your credit history is short or your score sits just under a lender’s cutoff.

These bills usually reach a credit report only when one goes unpaid and lands in collections, the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau says.

Boost doesn’t wait for the phone tech giant or utility to report. It reads two years of payments in the account you connect and lets you pick which qualifying bills go on your Experian report. Experian indicates you right away whether your FICO Score 8, one version of the FICO score, went up.

Only your Experian report gets those payments, so lenders checking your reports at the other two credit bureaus, Equifax and TransUnion, won’t see the gain. Experian also says not every lender uses a score that Boost affects, and most mortgage lenders don’t.

Payments by check or through apps like Venmo don’t count. Some rent paid online counts too, though Boost is just one of several ways to get rent reported. You also need enough history for a FICO Score, meaning at least one account active six months or more and one reported in the last six.

Sources indicate that take a renter with one credit card who links the account she pays her phone and electric bills from. Boost finds two years of on-time payments on both. Experian claims people whose score rose gained 14 points on average. The trade-off is letting Experian see that account’s payment history. Some scores also stay flat or even drop. If hers drops, she can disconnect, and Experian says the score should return to where it was.

Connect your bill-paying account now, ahead of any credit application, and leave it linked so Experian keeps checking for fresh on-time payments.
